newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-NORMAN CHARGES TO THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN CHARGES TO THE TOP.

text.p: Australian Greg Norman is poised to regain the world top ranking in some style after charging into the third round lead at the Spanish Open on Saturday.
Norman, 42, lost his world top ranking to American Tom Lehman last Sunday after a record 96-week spell but can probably reclaim it with a top-10 finish at La Moraleja on Sunday.
And after he mastered a windy day better than all his rivals for a four-under-par 68, he seems certain to achieve it easily.

On nine-under-par 207, he is one ahead of four players, second round leader Mark James of England, Dutchman Rolf Muntz, who led for much of the day before an indifferent last few holes, and two more Englishmen, David Howell and Peter Mitchell.
Dane Thomas Bjorn, looking for a substantial prize to try to move up a place from fourth spot in the European Ryder Cup table, is joint sixth with a large group on 209.
Norman is no disciple of the world rankings but has agreed that he would like the top ranking back.

Admitting surprise that he had moved through the field to lead, Norman gave himself another target. "I've won a lot of national titles but I've never won a Spanish Open, so it would be great to have one in the trophy case," he said.
"I did expect someone to lead on 12 or 13 under, but I guess the wind made it difficult. It can rattle your confidence and that was why I hit a few three woods today instead of drivers.
"The greens have still given me one or two problems because, with their combination of grasses, they are so difficult to read.
"I putted better today because I told myself to stop analysing why some putts can defy gravity and go uphill or I guess I'd have driven myself crazy.

"I had at least four three-footers coming back to save and I'm going to try to avoid that in the last round because it's too nerve-wracking. That's not to say that I'll have nerve problems. I can still jump in the cage with the sharks!"
Muntz took over the lead from James with three birdies to the 11th but a bogey on 14 enabled Norman to snatch it from the Dutchman, who had to settle for a round of 70.
Spaniards Jose Maria Olazabal and Severiano Ballesteros both faded. Olazabal had problems with the greens and dropped back to two-under 214 after a 74.
Ballesteros, whose nephew carried his bag after he sacked his caddie on Friday, had his third double-bogey in three rounds for a 73 to finish on 216.
